ruling: Q3 -- correction RECORD, artefact UNTOUCHED. No _v1 file was edited by this unit.
scope_discipline: This document carries ONLY the fields CORRECTIONS.md SS33 names, plus the supersedes and correction_record pointers the dispatch requires. It is a DELTA, not a re-issue of the whole artefact: every field of the _v1 not named below stands unchanged and the _v1 remains the artefact of record for them.
quoting_discipline: Dispatch reading (d): QUOTE VERBATIM OR DO NOT QUOTE. Every corrected quote below was re-anchored by V5 against the AUTHORS' OWN LaTeX e-print source fetched today, not against pdftotext output. That choice eliminates the defect class of D3 (a pdftotext line-break hyphenation carried into an artefact as verbatim) at the root.

corrections.defect_per_SS33: attribution: the second failing clause is verbatim but describes PRIOR WORK [69], not the paper's own construction
corrections.now: Section 1.1.2 'Imploding solutions', p.4 -- ATTRIBUTION: this sentence describes PRIOR WORK, not this paper's own construction. It sits inside a paragraph whose subject is reference [69]; the paragraph opens 'In the  work \cite{MeRaRoSz19c}, the authors used the solutions of \cite{MeRaRoSz19a} in order to show that ...' (LaTeX source line 203). [69] = \cite{MeRaRoSz19c} = Frank Merle, Pierre Raphaël, Igor Rodnianski, and Jeremie Szeftel, 'On the implosion of a compressible fluid II: singularity formation', Ann. of Math. (2) 196(2):779-889, 2022 (LaTeX source \bibitem line 6738).
corrections.attribution_verified_independently_by_V5: The bracket number was not taken on trust. V5 counted \bibitem occurrences in the authors' own LaTeX source up to and including MeRaRoSz19c: it is bibitem number 69, matching SS33's '[69]' exactly.
corrections.why_the_verdict_is_untouched: V3's FIRST failing clause is the paper's own voice and is character-exact as banked. V5 re-anchored it against the LaTeX source: 'In this section, we will study the linearized operator of the Euler equations around the self-similar profiles we have found. The stability for the Euler equation will follow in general, while in the Navier-Stokes case we need to restrict the parameter $r$ to a regime where the self-similar profile dominates the dissipation.' -- Section 7 'Linear Stability of the Profile', opening, LaTeX source line 2085. CONFIRMED verbatim. The Grade-B reading rests on this clause alone and is unaffected.

beyond_SS33_flagged_not_smuggled.what: the banked failing_clause_second_quoted has a SINGLE space in 'can be treated' where the authors' source has a DOUBLE space: 'can be  treated as exponentially decaying forcing'.
